title: Exclude old evidence before rebuilding
question: Can a late worker publish an obsolete generation?
scope: Toy single-file index: generation labels r17, r18, and r19. Atomic source-commit/exclusion coordination is one declared transaction; no physical timing or search-quality claim.

steps.title: Read a current index
steps.explanation: The source and indexed generation agree.

snapshot.result: r17 is admissible before the edit.

steps.title: Commit r18 with coordinated exclusion
steps.explanation: The commit transaction advances source identity and excludes its obsolete entries.

snapshot.result: The r17 bytes remain resident but cannot enter current evidence.

transition.meaning: The commit transaction advances source identity and excludes its obsolete entries.

steps.title: Build a private r18 candidate
steps.explanation: The worker completes a candidate outside the published index.

snapshot.result: Build completion alone does not publish r18.

transition.meaning: The worker completes a candidate outside the published index.

steps.title: Answer during the refresh window
steps.explanation: A bounded authorized source read supplies current bytes; the broader semantic search remains incomplete.

snapshot.result: No r17 entry is admitted as current.

transition.meaning: A bounded authorized source read supplies current bytes; the broader semantic search remains incomplete.

steps.title: Commit r19 before r18 publication
steps.explanation: A newer source transaction supersedes the worker generation.

snapshot.result: The completed r18 candidate is now obsolete.

transition.meaning: A newer source transaction supersedes the worker generation.

steps.title: Reject the stale worker at publication
steps.explanation: Atomic conditional publication compares the candidate against the current source generation.

snapshot.result: The published index still holds excluded r17; r18 cannot re-enter it.

transition.meaning: Atomic conditional publication compares the candidate against the current source generation.

steps.title: Release the rejected candidate
steps.explanation: No publisher or recovery reader references the rejected candidate.

snapshot.result: The obsolete worker allocation is free.

transition.meaning: No publisher or recovery reader references the rejected candidate.

invariants: Source and representation generations remain separate identities.
Build completion and index publication are separate boundaries.
Direct reads supply only their bounded observed source scope.

paragraphs: Original case follows coordinated exclusion through a superseded worker. Unchecked background publication uses the same two source edits and deliberately exposes stale admission and publication. Synchronous write-path rebuilding uses the first edit only and withholds write completion until current indexed evidence exists. These cases compare causal boundaries, not measured latency.

variants.label: Unchecked background publication
variants.scope: Deliberately unsafe comparison: same source edits and worker as Original case, but no admission exclusion or atomic generation check. Stale evidence is intentionally exposed.

steps.title: Read a current index
steps.explanation: The source and indexed generation agree.

snapshot.result: r17 is admissible before the edit.

steps.title: Commit r18 without coordinated exclusion
steps.explanation: The source advances while the unchecked gateway keeps admitting its old r17 representation.

snapshot.result: The old representation remains admissible despite the known source edit.

transition.meaning: The source advances while the unchecked gateway keeps admitting its old r17 representation.

steps.title: Build a private r18 candidate
steps.explanation: The worker completes a candidate outside the published index.

snapshot.result: Build completion alone does not publish r18.

transition.meaning: The worker completes a candidate outside the published index.

steps.title: Admit the stale r17 query result
steps.explanation: Without a generation admission check, the query treats resident r17 as current.

snapshot.result: A fast response can still supply stale evidence.

transition.meaning: Without a generation admission check, the query treats resident r17 as current.

steps.title: Commit r19 before r18 publication
steps.explanation: A newer source transaction supersedes the worker generation.

snapshot.result: The unchecked gateway still admits r17 while a second source edit supersedes the r18 worker.

transition.meaning: A newer source transaction supersedes the worker generation.

steps.title: Publish the superseded r18 worker
steps.explanation: This deliberately unsafe policy omits the atomic generation comparison.

snapshot.result: The index now contains r18 while the authoritative source is r19.

transition.meaning: This deliberately unsafe policy omits the atomic generation comparison.

steps.title: Release the worker staging candidate
steps.explanation: No publisher or recovery consumer still references the worker staging candidate.

snapshot.result: The obsolete r18 index persists after the worker candidate is released.

transition.meaning: No publisher or recovery consumer still references the worker staging candidate.

variants.label: Synchronous write-path rebuild
variants.scope: Same initial r17 and first source edit to r18. This comparison withholds write completion until current representations are published; no second source edit is injected and no physical latency is modeled.

steps.title: Read a current index
steps.explanation: The source and indexed generation agree.

snapshot.result: r17 is admissible before the edit.

steps.title: Commit r18 and withhold write completion
steps.explanation: Synchronous maintenance holds this caller at the write boundary until r18 representations are published.

snapshot.result: The caller cannot issue its dependent query while rebuilding is pending.

transition.meaning: The commit transaction advances source identity and excludes its obsolete entries.

steps.title: Build a private r18 candidate
steps.explanation: The worker completes a candidate outside the published index.

snapshot.result: The completed candidate still requires publication before write acknowledgment.

transition.meaning: The worker completes a candidate outside the published index.

steps.title: Publish current r18 and acknowledge the write
steps.explanation: A conditional publication transaction installs the current candidate and completes the synchronous write boundary.

snapshot.result: The dependent query can now use current indexed evidence.

transition.meaning: A conditional publication transaction installs the current candidate and completes the synchronous write boundary.

steps.title: Issue the dependent query after the rebuild
steps.explanation: The caller resumes only after synchronous maintenance publishes r18.

snapshot.result: This write path pays the rebuild delay before the dependent query.

transition.meaning: The caller resumes only after synchronous maintenance publishes r18.

title: One effect across a lost reply
question: Why does a retry need a new attempt ID but the same operation ID?
scope: Toy authorized endpoint, caller C and resource R, active retention window. The effect and its deduplication result commit atomically; real endpoints must declare whether that coupling is supported.

steps.title: Create one operation identity
steps.explanation: The operation identifies one intended payload, independently of transport attempts.

snapshot.result: No endpoint effect has occurred.

steps.title: Commit effect and retained result
steps.explanation: The endpoint finds no record and atomically applies payload X with its deduplication result.

snapshot.result: One effect has committed, whether its reply arrives or not.

transition.meaning: The endpoint finds no record and atomically applies payload X with its deduplication result.

steps.title: Lose the reply after commit
steps.explanation: The caller records transport uncertainty without changing endpoint state.

snapshot.result: Timeout does not mean the effect failed.

transition.meaning: The caller records transport uncertainty without changing endpoint state.

steps.title: Send another attempt of the same operation
steps.explanation: The caller preserves op-A and changes only the transport attempt identity.

snapshot.result: The retry still names the original intended effect.

transition.meaning: The caller preserves op-A and changes only the transport attempt identity.

steps.title: Read the retained result
steps.explanation: The endpoint recognizes the same scoped operation and payload inside retention.

snapshot.result: The effect count remains unchanged.

transition.meaning: The endpoint recognizes the same scoped operation and payload inside retention.

steps.title: Send a conflicting payload under op-A
steps.explanation: This request reuses an active operation identity with different arguments.

snapshot.result: The endpoint must compare payload binding before execution.

transition.meaning: This request reuses an active operation identity with different arguments.

steps.title: Reject the mismatched payload
steps.explanation: The endpoint refuses payload Y and preserves the original result.

snapshot.result: Neither a retry nor a conflict causes a new effect.

transition.meaning: The endpoint refuses payload Y and preserves the original result.

invariants: Every attempt requires independent authorization.
Completed duplicate and payload-conflict branches do not apply a new effect.
After retention expiry, this example establishes no repeat-safety guarantee.

title: Retain a prefix and rotate the suffix
question: Which bytes disappear when a full tail receives more output?
scope: Toy six ASCII bytes, head capacity 2 and tail capacity 3. Each action ingests one ready byte; channels alternate in observed readiness-loop order, which does not imply channel causality. Tail slots display chronological order. Status and notice framing have a separate reserved budget.

steps.title: Start draining both channels
steps.explanation: The readiness loop services stdout and stderr under capture limits.

snapshot.result: Every payload slot is initially unwritten.

steps.title: Ingest out:A
steps.explanation: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

snapshot.result: This byte remains retained; no retained tail byte counts as omitted.

transition.meaning: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

steps.title: Ingest err:b
steps.explanation: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

snapshot.result: This byte remains retained; no retained tail byte counts as omitted.

transition.meaning: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

steps.title: Ingest out:C
steps.explanation: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

snapshot.result: This byte remains retained; no retained tail byte counts as omitted.

transition.meaning: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

steps.title: Ingest err:d
steps.explanation: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

snapshot.result: This byte remains retained; no retained tail byte counts as omitted.

transition.meaning: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

steps.title: Ingest out:E
steps.explanation: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

snapshot.result: This byte remains retained; no retained tail byte counts as omitted.

transition.meaning: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

steps.title: Ingest err:f
steps.explanation: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

snapshot.result: The head remains fixed; only a byte evicted from the full tail increments omission.

transition.meaning: One ready byte enters capture: fill the head until full, then append to the tail; evict its oldest byte only when full.

steps.title: Serialize the bounded observation
steps.explanation: After confirmed process exit, stage status, retained prefix, measured omission, and chronological suffix.

snapshot.result: The nonzero exit status and measured omission remain explicit.

transition.meaning: After confirmed process exit, stage status, retained prefix, measured omission, and chronological suffix.

invariants: Drained bytes equal retained payload bytes plus evicted bytes.
The full head never changes after its initial fill.
Continued draining does not require unbounded capture memory.
Output omission and execution outcome are separate facts.

title: Earn permission to reuse a sandbox
question: Why is an ended lease still unavailable to the next tenant?
scope: Toy instance with explicit authority, process, workspace, and host-queue obligations. Restore is a declared mechanism covering these domains; no scan is claimed to prove all possible residue absent.

steps.title: Start from verified standby
steps.explanation: The supervisor has confirmed the baseline restoration.

snapshot.result: The instance can receive a lease.

steps.title: Assign one trajectory lease
steps.explanation: Admission transfers the instance to one task and binds its authority.

snapshot.result: The instance leaves the ready reserve.

transition.meaning: Admission transfers the instance to one task and binds its authority.

steps.title: Execute task-owned work
steps.explanation: One admitted execution produces private edits and outstanding owned work.

snapshot.result: The next tenant cannot inherit these task-owned resources.

transition.meaning: One admitted execution produces private edits and outstanding owned work.

steps.title: End the lease and mark tainted
steps.explanation: Lease expiry removes permission to allocate this instance to another task.

snapshot.result: An ended lease does not mean cleanup has finished.

transition.meaning: Lease expiry removes permission to allocate this instance to another task.

steps.title: Fence old authority
steps.explanation: The enforcement layer revokes lease identities and prevents new work under them.

snapshot.result: Previously owned work still requires positive quiescence.

transition.meaning: The enforcement layer revokes lease identities and prevents new work under them.

steps.title: Confirm all owned work has stopped
steps.explanation: The supervisor confirms both child execution and pending host work are quiescent.

snapshot.result: Artifacts now have a stable export boundary.

transition.meaning: The supervisor confirms both child execution and pending host work are quiescent.

steps.title: Export the permitted artifact
steps.explanation: The task export policy permits only this patch from the frozen private state.

snapshot.result: Export does not reset the workspace.

transition.meaning: The task export policy permits only this patch from the frozen private state.

steps.title: Restore the declared baseline domains
steps.explanation: The trusted reset mechanism clears private state after permitted outputs are saved.

snapshot.result: Restoration must still be verified before standby admission.

transition.meaning: The trusted reset mechanism clears private state after permitted outputs are saved.

steps.title: Verify restoration and return to standby
steps.explanation: The supervisor confirms the declared reset mechanism completed across all covered domains.

snapshot.result: Only this verified ownership transfer makes the instance reusable.

transition.meaning: The supervisor confirms the declared reset mechanism completed across all covered domains.

invariants: No instance belongs to standby while owned work or old authority remains.
Export occurs after quiescence and before private-state release.
Any incomplete teardown or failed verification requires removal from service.

variants.label: Reset verification fails
variants.scope: Same task and teardown order; the restoration completion proof fails at verification. Quarantine removes the instance from service pending destruction.

steps.explanation: The supervisor cannot confirm the declared restoration mechanism completed; the instance is removed from service.

snapshot.result: The failed instance remains quarantined for destruction and cannot receive another lease.

title: Private edits over shared lower files
question: How can task A edit and hide files while task B keeps reading them?
scope: Toy file-level overlay with code and data files. Copy-up and the first write are separate inspectable actions. Whiteout is upper-layer metadata, not a deletion of lower bytes or a block snapshot.

steps.title: Resolve reads through each merged view
steps.explanation: Both empty uppers fall through to the same read-only lower files.

snapshot.result: Shared baseline bytes are visible in both workspaces.

steps.title: Copy the code file into A’s upper
steps.explanation: The first write requires a private file copy; the shared source remains unchanged.

snapshot.result: A now owns a writable copy with the same initial content.

transition.meaning: The first write requires a private file copy; the shared source remains unchanged.

steps.title: Write the private code copy
steps.explanation: The upper file shadows the lower code only in task A’s merged namespace.

snapshot.result: Task B still reads code:old.

transition.meaning: The upper file shadows the lower code only in task A’s merged namespace.

steps.title: Hide data with an upper whiteout
steps.explanation: Deleting the lower data file creates a private deletion marker rather than removing shared bytes.

snapshot.result: A sees data absent; B still reads data:base.

transition.meaning: Deleting the lower data file creates a private deletion marker rather than removing shared bytes.

steps.title: Discard A’s private upper after its lease
steps.explanation: With all task consumers stopped, releasing A’s private state exposes the lower files in a fresh merged view.

snapshot.result: The baseline and B’s view have remained constant throughout.

transition.meaning: With all task consumers stopped, releasing A’s private state exposes the lower files in a fresh merged view.

invariants: The lower file values never change.
Task B’s private upper and merged values never change.
A whiteout occupies upper metadata even though its merged path is absent.

title: Publish only a recoverable checkpoint
question: When does a captured pair become eligible for recovery?
scope: Toy checkpoints c0 and c1, immutable workspace ws-r18 and matching record boundary. Payload storage survives the declared host failure. Pending test-r18 and its reservation remain unresolved while replay folds recorded events only.

steps.title: Retain the prior published checkpoint
steps.explanation: c0 remains the eligible restore point before c1 is captured.

snapshot.result: No incomplete replacement can displace c0.

steps.title: Freeze a compatible pair
steps.explanation: The record and workspace are captured at the same declared boundary.

snapshot.result: A captured pair is not yet eligible for recovery.

transition.meaning: The record and workspace are captured at the same declared boundary.

steps.title: Finish durable payload storage
steps.explanation: Both components reach storage in the declared failure domain; the manifest remains c0.

snapshot.result: Durable bytes alone do not publish a restore point.

transition.meaning: Both components reach storage in the declared failure domain; the manifest remains c0.

steps.title: Commit the c1 manifest
steps.explanation: Authoritative publication follows payload durability.

snapshot.result: c1 is now eligible; c0 remains retained for active recovery paths.

transition.meaning: Authoritative publication follows payload durability.

steps.title: Restore the published compatible pair
steps.explanation: Recovery selects the payload named by the committed manifest.

snapshot.result: Record and workspace refer to the same boundary.

transition.meaning: Recovery selects the payload named by the committed manifest.

steps.title: Fold the durable suffix
steps.explanation: The reducer applies recorded intent and reservation without invoking the test.

snapshot.result: The operation and its reservation remain pending.

transition.meaning: The reducer applies recorded intent and reservation without invoking the test.

steps.title: Reject a mismatched recovery pair
steps.explanation: A proposed newer record refers to bytes absent from the older workspace.

snapshot.result: Recovery must fall back to a compatible published pair with its suffix.

transition.meaning: A proposed newer record refers to bytes absent from the older workspace.

steps.title: Release unreferenced capture staging
steps.explanation: Published payloads and active recovery paths retain their independent references.

snapshot.result: Only capture-owned staging is freed; published restore points persist.

transition.meaning: Published payloads and active recovery paths retain their independent references.

invariants: The manifest never names a payload before it is durable.
Reconstruction does not invoke tools or infer unrecorded outcomes.
Pending operations retain their reservations.

title: Rebuild obligations from durable events
question: What survives when the live trajectory record disappears?
scope: Toy complete authoritative prefix: TaskStarted, Authorized, BudgetReserved, ToolIntent test-r18. No ToolResult was recorded. Folding is deterministic state reconstruction, never tool replay.

steps.title: Keep durable history separate from live state
steps.explanation: The prefix contains an intent but no correlated result.

snapshot.result: The external outcome remains unresolved even before the crash.

steps.title: Lose the volatile record on a crash
steps.explanation: Host memory disappears while the durable authoritative prefix survives.

snapshot.result: The operation identity and reservation are still recoverable.

transition.meaning: Host memory disappears while the durable authoritative prefix survives.

steps.title: Fold TaskStarted
steps.explanation: The deterministic reducer initializes the fresh task record.

snapshot.result: No external action is invoked.

transition.meaning: The deterministic reducer initializes the fresh task record.

steps.title: Fold the authorization
steps.explanation: The recorded admission applies to this task and operation.

snapshot.result: Recorded authority does not establish an external outcome.

transition.meaning: The recorded admission applies to this task and operation.

steps.title: Fold the owned reservation
steps.explanation: The reducer reconstructs the reservation itself, not merely a remaining balance.

snapshot.result: Its owner remains test-r18.

transition.meaning: The reducer reconstructs the reservation itself, not merely a remaining balance.

steps.title: Fold the unresolved intent
steps.explanation: The prefix contains no result that could settle test-r18.

snapshot.result: Recovery retains the operation and its reservation without rerunning it.

transition.meaning: The prefix contains no result that could settle test-r18.

invariants: The authoritative log remains unchanged during reconstruction.
A missing recorded result does not prove success, failure, or non-execution.
No tool invocation occurs while folding events.

title: Hold dispatch behind the durable intent
question: Why can a durable intent still be an unsent, in-doubt action?
scope: Toy authorized test-r18 attempt against immutable ws-r18. The complete authoritative prefix and receipt acknowledgment survive the declared failure domain; pending evidence does not settle the result.

steps.title: Start with an unsent proposal
steps.explanation: The request has not crossed admission or durability barriers.

snapshot.result: No external effect can follow from this attempt yet.

steps.title: Record the validated proposal
steps.explanation: The complete immutable proposal identifies operation test-r18 and its input.

snapshot.result: Validation alone permits no dispatch.

transition.meaning: The complete immutable proposal identifies operation test-r18 and its input.

steps.title: Record admission and its reservation
steps.explanation: A single admission transaction records permission and holds the operation budget.

snapshot.result: The request remains unsent while the intent barrier is pending.

transition.meaning: A single admission transaction records permission and holds the operation budget.

steps.title: Make the intent durable
steps.explanation: Storage persists the recoverable intent, but the worker has not received its acknowledgment.

snapshot.result: A lost acknowledgment would leave durable intent with dispatch withheld.

transition.meaning: Storage persists the recoverable intent, but the worker has not received its acknowledgment.

steps.title: Receive the durability acknowledgment
steps.explanation: The worker learns that intent and its required predecessors satisfy the declared durability contract.

snapshot.result: The operation can still be withheld; durable permission is not an obligation to dispatch.

transition.meaning: The worker learns that intent and its required predecessors satisfy the declared durability contract.

steps.title: Recheck admission and release the request
steps.explanation: A successful final control recheck permits this same admitted attempt to cross the network boundary.

snapshot.result: Until adequate outcome evidence is recorded, recovery treats the operation as in doubt.

transition.meaning: A successful final control recheck permits this same admitted attempt to cross the network boundary.

steps.title: Record a pending observation
steps.explanation: The evidence is correlated but does not establish a final outcome.

snapshot.result: The reservation remains held; timeout or pending is not settlement.

transition.meaning: The evidence is correlated but does not establish a final outcome.

steps.title: Record adequate correlated outcome evidence
steps.explanation: The endpoint-specific evidence establishes the test outcome within its declared contract.

snapshot.result: Downstream work may use the recorded result; reservation settlement is a separate action.

transition.meaning: The endpoint-specific evidence establishes the test outcome within its declared contract.

invariants: No dispatch occurs before acknowledgment of recoverable intent.
The same admitted reservation persists through acknowledgment and dispatch.
Pending evidence never establishes a completed outcome.
An absent intent establishes non-dispatch only in a complete authoritative prefix.
